title: Practical Absolute Entropies of Gases Can Be Calculated from Partition Functions
lead: The entropy of a system can be written in terms of its partition function. Near absolute zero only the lowest levels are occupied, so the sum over states keeps only its first terms, and the formula can be tested against the third law.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercise on this section, so the exercise, its solution, Bloom level and concept tags are written by AI. The numeric answer accepts a 2% tolerance.

exercises.source_id: If the ground state is $n$ degenerate
exercises.prompt: One mole of a molecular crystal is cooled toward 0 K. Each molecule has a doubly degenerate ground level and the molecules are independent, so the ground state of the crystal is $2^{N_A}$-fold degenerate. What entropy does the crystal keep as $\kT \to 0$?

answer.hint: Take the low-temperature limit $S \to k_B\ln n$ with $n = 2^{N_A}$, and use $N_Ak_B = R$.
answer.solution: As $\kT \to 0$ the entropy goes to $k_B\ln n$, and here $n = 2^{N_A}$. So $S \to k_B\ln 2^{N_A} = N_Ak_B\ln 2 = (1\ \text{mol})(8.314\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1})(0.6931) = 5.76$ J/K. The crystal keeps this entropy at 0 K because its ground state is not single.

footnotes.html: The book stops at the sum over levels and never takes the limit. As $\kT \to 0$, $S \to k_B\ln n$, which is zero for a ground state that is not degenerate; the derivation after the sum works the steps.
For an $n$-fold degenerate ground state the last of the equal energies is $E_n$, so the line reads $\kEone = E_2 = \dots = E_n$; the book prints $E_m$.

derivations.source: Physical Chemistry (LibreTexts), 21.6 Practical Absolute Entropies of Gases Can Be Calculated from Partition Functions

steps.cap: The logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms, and $\ln e^{a} = a$.
$\ln n$ does not change with $\kT$, and the derivative of $-\kEone/k_B\kT$ with respect to $\kT$ is $\kEone/k_B\kT^2$.

nodes.note: The book writes the derivative with $\delta$; it is the partial derivative $\partial$.

assumes.text: The next level lies above the ground level, $E_{n+1} > \kEone$.

steps.cap: With $E_{n+1}-\kEone > 0$, each $e^{-(E_{n+1}-\kEone)/k_B\kT}$ goes to zero faster than any power of $\kT$. The logarithm goes to $\ln 1$, and $k_B\kT$ times its derivative, about $\frac{m}{n}\frac{E_{n+1}-\kEone}{\kT}e^{-(E_{n+1}-\kEone)/k_B\kT}$, goes to zero too.

assumes.text: A perfect crystal has a single ground state, $n = 1$.
